title: Nat.em_implies_lpo: excluded middle yields the limited principle of omniscience over the naturals
statement: Written over a Bool-valued sequence f : Nat -> Bool, which is Bishop's formulation: Hits f := exists n, f n = true ("f fires somewhere") and Misses f := forall n, f n = false ("f never fires"). LPO is forall f, Or (Hits f) (Misses f); WLPO is forall f, Or (Misses f) (Not (Misses f)); Markov's principle (MP) is forall f, Not (Misses f) -> Hits f; LLPO is forall f g, Not (And (Hits f) (Hits g)) -> Or (Misses f) (Misses g); EM is forall (P : Prop), Or P (Not P). This fact is the top edge of the reverse-mathematics map (roadmap W1-9): from excluded middle as an explicit hypothesis, LPO follows. Excluded middle is used exactly ONCE, at the single proposition `Hits f`; turning the negative branch into `Misses f` is a Bool.rec case split on f n, a genuine two-constructor elimination and not a second appeal to omniscience. THE PRINCIPLE IS A HYPOTHESIS, NOT AN AXIOM. It is spelled out inline in the type -- never behind a Definition -- so a reader of the rendered statement sees the whole assumption and nothing about the conclusion can be smuggled into an abbreviation. That is why axiom_footprint is empty. ADR-1601 (roadmap W0-2) decides this policy and prices it: across the ten theorems of this family the hypothesis route costs 11 binders and 14 argument positions and ZERO proof obligations. WHAT THIS FACT DOES NOT CLAIM: it does not claim the principle in its hypothesis is true, false, or independent. The SEPARATIONS in the standard picture -- LPO is not constructively derivable, LLPO does not give LPO, WLPO does not give LPO, MP does not give WLPO -- are CITED here (Bishop, Constructive Analysis ch. 1) and are not proved: each needs a model of this kernel rather than a term in it, and ADR-1600 records why an internal metatheorem about this kernel is unavailable.

formal.statement: theorem Nat.em_implies_lpo : ((x0 : ((x0 : Prop) -> Or x0 (Not x0))) -> ((x1 : ((x1 : AxNat) -> Bool)) -> Or (Exists.{1} AxNat (fun (x2 : AxNat) => Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x2) Bool.true)) (((x2 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} Bool (x1 x2) Bool.false))))

evidence.supports: Nat.em_implies_lpo is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example kernel_declaration_projection -- --require-declaration Nat.em_implies_lpo --require-kind theorem
evidence.notes: --require-declaration exits non-zero when the name is absent from every constructed prelude, and --require-kind exits non-zero when it is present with the wrong kind, so the exit status depends on the finding rather than on the run completing. --release is MANDATORY: this binary builds creal/complex/cpoint, which overflow the default debug thread stack.

Anchored with [[:space:]]-free literals, never \t -- in a scripted (GNU) grep \t is a literal t.

notes: Extends the single calibration point least_number.rs established (F:nat-lnp-unrestricted-implies-em, F:nat-lnp-decidable) into a map. The NON-VACUITY anchor for this family is that the BOUNDED forms are already theorems here: Nat.lnp_bounded_search and Nat.lnp_decidable prove, axiom-free, that a bounded search over a Bool-valued predicate finds its least witness. So the search machinery is present and works; what LPO adds is exactly the unbounded decision. Source: crates/axeyum-lean-kernel/src/nat_prelude/omniscience.rs.
